title: Press culture tube snap caps to their vented first stop
instruction: Snap a cap onto each of the three culture tubes in the rack, pressed only to its first (vented) stop so the cultures get air overnight.
context: Done by: microbiologists (O*NET 19-1022.00; 20,100 US workers in 2025), whose O*NET tasks include keeping bacterial cultures under controlled aeration, and biological technicians (19-4021.00; 74,400), per O*NET OnLine (BLS 2025 data). Setting up overnight E. coli cultures in 14 mL round-bottom tubes is daily molecular-biology bench work; protocols say to cover the culture with a cap that is not airtight before 12-18 h of shaking at 37 C. On these tubes the two-position snap cap makes that loose state a defined first click (vented); the second click seals the tube airtight (the position meant for anaerobic culture). Unlike seating a cap fully home, success is the intermediate click: each cap must go square onto the tube mouth and be pressed a few millimetres only, then released.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left); z from the table top. Rack, fixed: teal polypropylene 3-place rack for 17 mm tubes, 5.6 x 16.0 x 6.2 cm, centred at (30.0, 0.0), wells at y = +5.0, 0.0 and -5.0. Culture tubes, held upright in the three wells: 14 mL round-bottom clear polypropylene tubes, 17 mm x 100 mm, each with about 3 mL of amber LB broth, blue printed graduations and a white writing patch, open (no cap). Bench pad, fixed: 11.0 x 11.0 x 0.2 cm absorbent bench-protector square (white quilted absorbent top, blue polyethylene backing) centred at (24.0, -18.0). Caps, loose: three natural (off-white) low-density polyethylene two-position snap caps for these tubes, 21.2 mm across the top flange, 20 mm tall, hollow skirt 19.2 mm inside, 5 g each, standing open-side down on the pad at (21.5, -18.0), (25.5, -20.4) and (25.5, -15.6). Nothing else is on the bench.
scoring: Measured per tube with a ruler and a side photo. A tube counts when a cap stands upright on it (tilted 20 degrees or less), centred on the tube within 5 mm, and pressed 4-6 mm further down than a cap just set on the tube (the vented first stop, nominal 5 mm: cap top about 108.5 mm above the table instead of 113.5 mm). A cap just set on the tube (pressed less than 4 mm), pressed more than 6 mm (the sealed second stop is at about 9 mm), tilted more than 20 degrees or off-centre does not count for that tube. On real tubes, take the first-stop height from a spare tube clicked to its first stop and count caps within 1 mm of it. Score at the end of the run = counted tubes / 3: 0 (no tube counts, or the rack or any tube is tilted more than 20 degrees), 0.33 (one tube), 0.67 (two tubes, or three while any of the three caps still moves at 3 cm/s or more or turns at 0.3 rad/s or more), 1.0 (three tubes with all three caps still: under 3 cm/s and under 0.3 rad/s). A successful run ends after the 1.0 state has held for 1 s.
reset_notes: Pull any cap off its tube (it pulls back over both stops), and stand the three caps open-side down on the pad at (21.5, -18.0), (25.5, -20.4) and (25.5, -15.6).
fidelity: Tube and cap at real size. The cap's two stops are a contact detent: two rows of four spring-loaded rollers in the tube wall and a chamfered inner lip in the cap. About 1 N snaps the lip over the upper row to the vented stop at 5 mm; 4-5 N snaps it over the lower row to the sealed stop at 9 mm. Springs and contact only, no code holds the cap (travel, forces: our estimates). Rack holds tubes fixed; broth static. Each cap is about 24 px at 1280x704; proxy: SUBACTION_END log, end close-ups.
